dedupe_keys.name: household economy approach livelihood zone profiles for six sahel countries 2011 2018

description: These workbooks describe how rural households in six Sahel countries get their food and income, zone by zone, which is the baseline humanitarian agencies use to judge how a drought or price rise will hit food security. The producers are Daniel Mardi, Celia Petty and Rosalind Cornforth of the Walker Institute, now The Pearl, at the University of Reading, who compiled Household Economy Approach profiles for livelihood zones mapped by the Famine Early Warning Systems Network. Coverage is Senegal, Mali, Burkina Faso, Niger, Nigeria and Chad, with profiles from 2011 to 2018. Each zone lists the crops grown and their seasonal calendars and, for each wealth group, the main sources of food and cash income and the main expenditures, with notes on markets, hazards and coping strategies where available. The workbooks and documentation are available as a free download from Zenodo under the Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 licence. Caveats: profiles describe a reference year and may be outdated, detail varies between countries, and zones are broad areas, not villages. Simulation uses: setting household food source and market dependence in food security and humanitarian response models, and estimating which zones lose food access after drought or flood. Related records: the FEWS NET data explorer (data-fews-net-data-explorer) publishes current food security outlooks and the livelihood zone maps.
